body.statement:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the local quadratic kernels lift to a symmetric matrix \(A_n\) on the common ambient observed array such that
\[
 Q-B_2=\epsilon^{\top}A_n\epsilon
 -\mathbb E[\epsilon^{\top}A_n\epsilon\mid M,\Omega]
\]
and
\[
 |Q-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\ell_n^4}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\sqrt n}\right).
\]
The cubic, polar/regularization, scalar-resolvent, and native--auxiliary terms in the signed aggregate obey
\[
 |R_{\mathrm{agg}}|=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left[
 \ell_n^4\left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}
 +n^{-3/2}\right\}\right].
\]
These are centered aggregate bounds; they do not follow by summing pointwise absolute errors.
body.proof_tex:
For each target, the map \(e\mapsto q_{it}(e)\) is a homogeneous quadratic form. Extend its coefficient matrix by zero from the ordered local observed chart to \(I\times J\), symmetrize it, average over \(gH\), and call the resulting ambient matrix \(A_n\). This construction gives identically
\[
 Q=\epsilon^{\top}A_n\epsilon,
 \qquad B_2=\mathbb E(\epsilon^{\top}A_n\epsilon\mid M,\Omega),
\tag{26}
\]
so the first displayed identity is not an approximation.

The restricted Gram bounds and incoherence imply
\[
 \max_{i,j,t}|a_{ij,t}|\le C/n,
 \qquad \max_{t,s}|b_{t,s}|\le C/n,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j\in C(t)}a_{ij,t}^2+sum_{s\in S}b_{t,s}^2\le C/n.
\tag{27}
\]
The last term of the complete tangent has coefficient \(a_{ij,t}b_{t,s}\), including its negative sign. Substituting all three blocks of \(\ell_{it}\) into the rowwise Hessian bound (16), aggregating equal ambient coordinates before taking norms, and using (27) gives
\[
 \|A_n\|_F^2\le\frac{C}{n\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2},
 \qquad
 \max_u\sum_v |(A_n)_{uv}|le\frac C{n\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}},
 \qquad
 |\operatorname{tr}(A_n\Gamma_q)|\le\frac C{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}.
\tag{28}
\]
If the negative overlap block is omitted, the first two contractions in (28) contain an uncancelled donor--pre row sum; thus (28) specifically uses the complete tangent formula.

Truncate the errors at \(K\ell_n\) and recenter them conditionally. By (2) and a union bound over \(NT=O(n^2)\), the truncation changes (26) with probability \(O(n^{-6})\). Color calendar time by residues modulo \(2q+1\). Within a row, vertices of a fixed color are separated by more than \(q\), and different rows are conditionally independent. In the variance expansion of the centered quadratic form, two coefficient pairs have zero covariance unless the graph formed by their four row--time vertices has no isolated dependency component. Exposing one coefficient pair and then its finitely many possible row/time neighbors, (28) gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[(Q-B_2)^2\mid M,\Omega\right]
 \le \frac{C_qK^4\ell_n^8}{n\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}.
\tag{29}
\]
Chebyshev's inequality proves the quadratic bound.

It remains to control the aggregate of the remainders defined in the implicit-expansion lemma. Write every integral Taylor term as a multilinear kernel in the original ambient errors, aggregate equal monomials first, and take its Hoeffding decomposition relative to the independent rows and the \((2q+1)\)-coloring within each row. A nondegenerate degree-one projection changes a tangent coefficient by at most \(C\ell_n^2\sqrt n/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2\); keep this difference inside \(R_{\mathrm{agg}}\), while the declared \(L\) itself remains unchanged. The coefficient calculation using (27), (16)--(17), and \(h_{it}\le C/n\) is
\[
 |\mathbb E R_k|+|R_k-\mathbb E R_k\|_2
 \le C\ell_n^4
 \left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}+n^{-3/2}\right\}
 \rho_n^{,k-3},
 \qquad k\ge3,
\tag{30}
\]
where \(R_k\) denotes the degree-\(k\) projection component and \(\rho_n\) is (10). Equation (30) follows by pairing every nonfree vertex of a degenerate monomial with a vertex in the same row and within \(q\) dates: two free factor sums cost at most \(n\), the aggregate normalization contributes \((gH)^{-1}\), and (27) contributes one \(n^{-1/2}\) for each unpaired tangent leg. The Hessian or third-resolvent denominator contributes \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^{-2}\). Terms containing the residual polar factor have two target leverages and satisfy the second term in braces because
\[
 \lambda n^{-2}=O(n^{-3/2}\ell_n).
\tag{31}
\]
This is a coefficient enumeration of the common ambient polynomial, not a pointwise Lipschitz bound.

Because \(\rho_n=o(1)\), summing (30) over \(k\ge3\), adding the polar and scalar-resolvent pieces from (31), and finally adding the native--auxiliary discrepancy proved in \(\mathrm{lem:neighborhood\mbox{-}native\mbox{-}coupling}\), gives
\[
 |R_{\mathrm{agg}}|le_{\mathbb P}C\ell_n^4
 \left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}+n^{-3/2}\right\}.
\tag{32}
\]
Equations (26), (29), and (32) prove the lemma.
